msg: RULING ADR 0026 P1b lock (one checkout, concurrent emitters): (A) never-drop guarantee = SELF-HEALING STAGING: every publish and every sync stages all of tics.d (git add -A tics.d), so a tic orphaned by any lost race is committed by the next emit/sync; never '|| return 0' past a failed commit — a failed commit leaves the tic in the worktree (the reader's union still sees it) and is retried. (B) correctness of the checkout = a short mkdir lock per bus checkout (portable, atomic; no flock on macOS) around LOCAL mutations only — add, commit, and the fetch+rebase of a rejected push — NEVER held across the push itself; stale lock broken when its recorded pid is dead or its age > 2x TICS_NET_TIMEOUT; a failed rebase always runs 'rebase --abort' so no rebase-in-progress state survives. (C) reject retry-on-index.lock as the primary: a busy-wait that doesn't cover a rebase interleaving with a commit. Pins: P1b (exists) + P1c: a crashed emitter's stale lock does not block the next emit beyond the age bound, and after a forced rebase failure the checkout is clean (no .git/rebase-merge).
